# Policy-KB bijection audit — energy_services_desk / task 0

Scope: the whole normative domain of the two extended policies this task exercises — `energy_ext_analyst_overage_charge` and `energy_ext_subscription_settlement_payment` — together with every base policy governing their subjects (`energy_analyst_services`, `energy_billing_and_late_fee`), their `overwrite` declarations, their baselines, all nine of their declared factors with every tier of every ladder, and the two task-tool contracts. Untriggered branches are audited equally with the branch this seed hits.

Corpus audited: `env/env_0002_commercial_hvac_service_contractor/docs/energy/*.json`, 63 documents, md5 of the per-file digest list `4edcc2605db28339cd729cc2344a6b89`. No document was edited.

## source_to_kb

### A. `energy_ext_analyst_overage_charge`

**Hub / trigger and effect.** Source `rule`, first sentence: "Analyst work drawn beyond the hours a subscription year includes is invoiced to the building owner as one charge on the subscription, covering the studies already delivered." Home: *Desk Tool Card — Invoicing Analyst Overage on an Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscription* (`analyst_overage_invoicing_2f005262.json`), "When the charge is raised", carried verbatim, followed by the state it brings about ("from that moment it stands on the subscription's invoice history and raises the amount the subscription owes"), which matches the tool's own effect in `task_tools.py` ("raising the amount the subscription owes by the amount entered and appearing on the subscription's invoice history from the moment it is accepted"). Equivalent at entailment.

**Baseline (`baseline.rule`).** Home: *Accounts Practice — Charge for Analyst Hours Beyond the Pool* (`analyst_hours_beyond_the_pool_charge_basis_d1a451bb.json`). Sentence by sentence:

| Source baseline sentence | Prose home | Judgement |
|---|---|---|
| "The chargeable hours are the hours that count toward the pool, less the hours the pool provides and less the grace allowance, and never less than nothing." | "The charge" §, verbatim | equivalent |
| "The charge is the chargeable hours taken at the analyst hour rate, rounded to the nearest cent once at the end, and it is never less than nothing." | same §, verbatim | equivalent |
| "The hours that count toward the pool are the analyst hours logged on studies delivered in the twelve months ending on the day the charge is worked out, other than the hours of rate analysis studies and of demand response settlement studies." | "The quantities" 1 | equivalent (adds only that each delivery record carries its day, class and hours — the evidence fields, not a new norm) |
| "The hours the pool provides are the analyst hours the tier includes for a subscription year." | "The quantities" 2 | equivalent |
| "No grace allowance is set against the chargeable hours." | "The quantities" 3 | equivalent |
| "The analyst hour rate is the rate the tier sets for analyst hours beyond the included pool." | "The quantities" 4 | equivalent |
| order of assembly (hours combined first, floored, then multiplied, one rounding) | "Order of the arithmetic" | equivalent |

`baseline.params` `analyst_hours_included_per_year` and `analyst_hour_rate_usd` are both named in the document as tier figures and both rendered in figures in *Energy Analyst Services Entitlement Card* (2.0/6.0/16.0/32.0/60.0/160.0 hours; 195/188/180/172/165/158 USD). The baseline therefore yields a definite number on its own. Nothing is added; no default is softened; no assembly step is displaced into a factor document.

The `pool_provided` and `analyst_hour_rate` documents both name the other product by its official name — "the plan the building holds under Building Automation Service Plans" — and the kinds of record they read ("support hours still standing for its plan year — a figure above nothing on that plan's record"; "the rate that plan sets for support hours … read from the plan"). **`overwrite`.** One declaration, against `energy_analyst_services`: the clause "The hours logged on a delivered study are drawn from the subscription year's pool, and once the pool is exhausted the further hours of that study and of every later study are billed at the tier's analyst hour rate." Home: *Analyst Group Practice Note — Study Delivery and the Hour Pool*, where it is quoted verbatim under "The following sentence of this note is **no longer in force**, having been superseded by the current basis for invoicing analyst work beyond the included hours, and is retained only so that it is not applied", together with the base `formula` `analyst_overage_usd` it carried ("together with the per-study overage arithmetic that accompanied it (the hours of a study beyond the pool at the tier's rate, rounded to the cent)"). Retired in the source, present in the KB, written as retired: correct on all three limbs.

**Base policy `energy_analyst_services`, clauses not retired.** All still carried as clauses in force in the same document: the delivery-standing and turnaround sentence, the not-split-across-the-boundary sentence, and the rate-maintenance / demand-response sentence with its per-tier table. Its measure `energy_msr_analyst_hours_used_year` is rendered ("The hours used in the subscription year are the hours logged on studies delivered from the first day of the term through its last day"), matching the measure's window and aggregate. Its eligibility `live_subscription_for_analysis` (state_contract allowed `active`, `pending_renewal`) is rendered at full strength ("a study is not delivered on a subscription in onboarding, suspended, expired, cancelled, quoted or declined status") — the enumeration is the complement of the allowed set over the product's lifecycle, an entailment rather than an addition. Per-tier params are in *Energy Analyst Services Entitlement Card*, all six rows checked against `variants`.

### B. `energy_ext_subscription_settlement_payment`

**Hub / trigger and effect.** Source `rule`: "A building owner who asks to settle an energy monitoring subscription in one payment is quoted the sum that clears it, and that sum is worked out from the subscription's own ledger rather than from the balance the dashboard displays" and "The sum is entered as one payment applied to the oldest invoice standing unpaid on the subscription, whatever else it clears." Home: *Customer Payment Card — Settling an Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscription in One Payment*, both verbatim; the first is also the opening of the baseline document *Statement Basis — The Sum that Clears an Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscription*, which is the same policy's own restatement, not a second policy's.

**Baseline (`baseline.rule`).** Home: *Statement Basis — The Sum that Clears an Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscription*:

| Source baseline sentence | Prose home | Judgement |
|---|---|---|
| "The amount owed is every charge invoiced on the subscription, less every payment received on it and less the credits set against it, and never less than nothing." | "The basis" 1 | equivalent |
| "The credits set against it are every credit standing on the subscription." | "The basis" 2 | equivalent |
| "No settlement allowance is granted against the amount owed." | "The basis" 3 | equivalent |
| "The allowance ceiling is the opening ceiling." | "The basis" 4, with the figure — "the opening ceiling, USD 60" | equivalent (`allowance_cap_new` rendered) |
| "The qualifying amount is the long cycle qualifying amount." | "The basis" 5, with the figure — "the long cycle qualifying amount, USD 6000" | equivalent (`threshold_annual` rendered) |
| "The settlement allowance is worked out on the amount owed at the allowance rate, rounded to the nearest cent, and it is never more than the allowance ceiling; it is granted only where the amount owed reaches the qualifying amount, and where the amount owed falls short of that amount no allowance is granted at all." | "The basis" 6, verbatim | equivalent |
| "The sum the owner settles is the amount owed less the settlement allowance, rounded to the nearest cent once at the end, and never less than nothing." | "The basis" 7, verbatim | equivalent |
| order (three ledger totals first, floor, qualify, allowance rounded then held to the ceiling, one final rounding, floor) | "Order of the arithmetic" | equivalent |

Both baseline params are rendered in figures, so this baseline also yields a definite number on its own.

**Declared factors:**

| `allowance_rate` (parameter) | *Terms Schedule — Settlement Allowance Rate by Payment Record* | 3 of 3 | "The record months are the 12 months …; the settled payment count is 3 payments. The clean record rate is 2 percent and the light record rate is 1 percent" (`record_months`, `payment_count_threshold`, `allowance_pct_clean`, `allowance_pct_light`) |
| `allowance_ceiling` (parameter) | *Desk Q&A — The Allowance Ceiling at Settlement* | 3 of 3, both parts of each compound condition intact (months run **and** active) | "The long standing count is 18 whole months and the established count is 6 whole months; the long standing ceiling is USD 250, the established ceiling USD 150 and the opening ceiling USD 60" (all six constants) |
| `qualifying_amount` (parameter) | *Accounts Schedule — The Qualifying Amount for a Settlement Allowance* | 3 of 3 | "The recent months are the 3 months …and the recent charge count is 3 charges. The short cycle qualifying amount is USD 500, the quiet cycle qualifying amount USD 1500 and the long cycle qualifying amount USD 6000" (all five constants) |

Each document states the day-field that places a row in its window ("Charges are placed in the window by the day the invoice carrying each fell due, payments by the day each was received in the office"; "A late charge is counted by the day the invoice carrying it fell due; a payment is counted by the day it was received"), matching the `date_field` of each compute binding. No tier is dropped, merged, rounded or softened; no threshold is named under a business term without its figure.

**`overwrite`.** One declaration, against `energy_billing_and_late_fee`: the clause "Credits — for a late report, for a shortfall paid as a credit, or for a billing adjustment — are applied to the next subscription invoice rather than refunded, except that a shortfall payment is made by cheque where the owner asks for one." Home: *Accounts Office Bulletin — Invoicing, Due Dates and Late Fees*, quoted verbatim under "Clause no longer in force … it is retained only so that it is not applied". Correct on all three limbs.

**Base policy `energy_billing_and_late_fee`, clauses not retired.** All carried as in force in the same document: the invoicing-together sentence, the due-date counting rule, the late fee per month or part month, "Analyst overages, meter overages and dashboard user overages are invoiced in the period they arise", and "Payments are applied to the oldest unpaid invoice unless the owner names one" (with its two-row table). Its `formula` `late_fee_usd` is rendered ("The late fee for one month or part month is the overdue amount multiplied by the tier's monthly late fee percentage, rounded to the nearest cent"). Per-tier params are in the *Billing Terms and Arrears Table*, all six rows checked against `variants` (billing frequency, payment terms, late fee percentage, plus the suspension, reinstatement and restart columns belonging to `energy_suspension_and_reinstatement`).

**Resolution basis at the source's strength.** The prerequisite sentence names the state "the charge owed for the analyst hours drawn beyond the year's included pool stands invoiced on the subscription". The depended-on policy's own rule, in its own document, describes the write that brings that state about in the same words: "Analyst work drawn beyond the hours a subscription year includes is invoiced to the building owner as one charge on the subscription … from that moment it stands on the subscription's invoice history and raises the amount the subscription owes." The records supply the rest: the invoice history carries a `charge_type` of the analyst overage kind with its due date, and the delivery record carries every study's hours, class, asking day and delivery day, so a reader can see both that hours have been drawn beyond the pool and that no charge for them stands. Strength matches: the source makes it a hard gate ("is fixed only after"), and the KB sentence is the same hard gate — not advisory, not combinable, not a hint.

## kb_to_source

Every normative claim in the two policies' documents and in the base documents governing their subjects was traced to a structured source. The following categories were checked specifically.

**Obligations, eligibility and prohibitions.** Traced: the delivery-standing gate (`energy_analyst_services.eligibility.live_subscription_for_analysis`), the quotation-instead rule for work the tier does not include (`energy_analyst_services.rule`), the payment-application rule and the due-date counting rule (`energy_billing_and_late_fee.rule`). No claim was found without a source.

**Calculations.** Every arithmetic statement in the nine factor documents and the two baseline documents maps to a `compute` binding and its `compute_basis` sentence. The worked examples are all flagged hypothetical ("Worked example (hypothetical inputs)", "Illustration (hypothetical)", "Boundary (hypothetical)") and use invented figures; none reproduces this task's world.

**Additions searched for and not found.** No "please confirm the amount/date with the customer", no "review again before handling", no "notify/verify after completion", no "if it fails, follow some procedure". A regex sweep of the energy corpus for pointer and route language (`unless otherwise`, `set out elsewhere`, `adjustments may`, `see the`, `refer to`, `as described in`, `first call`, `before this can`, `must be done first`, `checklist`, `roadmap`, `exception list`, `certain customers qualify`, `most customers`, `common mistake`, `the mistake`) returned two matches, both false positives on ordinary prose ("how many named users see the dashboard"; "the further step 20 percentage points"). Nothing normative was added.

**Prerequisite-side check 1 — cross-problem operational guidance.** None. `condition`, `resolved_by` and `effect` appear nowhere. Within the blocked problem's documents, no tool other than its own is named; within the depended-on problem's documents, the blocked side is not mentioned at all. Each of the six task tools is named in exactly one document, its own hub.

**Prerequisite-side check 2 — a task's opening world state written in as a policy fact.** None. A search of the energy corpus for this task's world (the company names, the site, the meter, invoice and study references, and every scored or intermediate figure — `Brightleaf`, `INV-401`, `ST-401`, `3118.5`, `5355.21`, `640318`, and the rest) returns no match. No document says anything of the form "this customer currently has arrears" or "no overage charge stands".

**Omissions.** None found. Every tier of every ladder, every baseline default and every base clause governing the two subjects has a prose home; the retired clauses are present and written as retired.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS** — no `KB-BIJECTION RED`.

- All 2 extended policies, their 2 baselines, their 9 factors (27 ladder tiers), their 2 `overwrite` declarations and the 2 base policies governing their subjects correspond losslessly at the level of entailment, including the branches this seed never triggers (a suspended subscription's credits, a late charge in the record window, a young or non-active term's ceiling, an annually-invoiced tier's qualifying amount, a semiannual/quarterly/no true-up gathering window, a tier keeping neither entitlement current, a young active term's prorated pool, the volume-step rate, and the opening and no grace allowances).
- The retired surface is correct on all three limbs for both declarations: nothing retired is stated as in force, nothing retired has vanished, and nothing is retired that the source did not declare retired.
- No prior revision of this file exists; this is revision 1.

**Policy-side notes (recorded, not part of this skill's verdict).**

1. **An open boundary in the source's prose.** The `billing_period` of the analyst overage charge is fixed by the source only through a base sentence ("Analyst overages, meter overages and dashboard user overages are invoiced in the period they arise") plus the tier's billing frequency. The KB carries both, so the documents are faithful; but the extended policy's own rule does not state the period, which leaves the spelling to be assembled by the reader rather than read off.
2. **A base formula overlapping an extended computation.** `energy_agg_portfolio_meter_pricing.formula.annual_fee_usd` is not retired by any `overwrite`, and is rendered in force in *Pricing Desk Note — Portfolio Meter Pricing* ("The annual fee of a subscription is the tier's annual subscription fee, plus the tier's per-meter fee multiplied by the meters the subscription covers, …"). It is a different arithmetic from `energy_ext_meter_coverage_amendment`'s amended annual fee. This bears on task 1 rather than task 0, and is recorded there as well; the KB rendering is faithful to the source in both places, so the question is one for the policy layer.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|

| Another problem's tool named inside a blocked problem's documents | **none.** `charge_analyst_overage_446fe12a` occurs only in *Invoicing Analyst Overage*; `settle_subscription_balance_535836bf` only in *Settling a Subscription in One Payment*. Each hub's invocation block names its own tool only, which is permitted. |
| A dependency or order between problems stated where no prerequisite sentence states it | **none.** No sentence in the analyst-overage documents says the settlement waits on it; no sentence elsewhere states the edge a second time. The corpus-wide search for the prerequisite sentence returns exactly one occurrence. |
| The source's edge stated in a second document | **none** (same search). |
| A document aggregating several problems' prerequisites into a table, checklist, roadmap or route | **none.** No document lists more than one problem's precondition; no document strings the two writes into an ordered step list. |
| Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call …") | **none.** |
| Contrast between a wrong and a correct reading, a named mistake, or an example walking across problems | **none.** Every example is a self-contained hypothetical inside one document's own rule; none crosses from one problem to another. |
| Title or opening mirroring a task's situation | **none.** Titles name general subjects — "The Amended Annual Fee of an Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscription", "Charge for Analyst Hours Beyond the Pool", "The Sum that Clears an Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscription". "Settling an Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscription in One Payment" names the request type that defines its `on_request` policy, which is that policy's general subject, not a mirror. No title names a caller, a building or a situation. |
| Depended-on document reachable only through the dependent document's phrasing | **no.** *Invoicing Analyst Overage* is reachable from the record vocabulary alone — the invoice history's own `analyst_overage` charge kind, and the delivery rows' hours and classes. |
| Factor document saying which tier a customer falls on, naming the reading to avoid, or writing a task's evidence rows in as fact | **none** across all nine. Each states its ladder as a rule and leaves the tier to be derived; the illustrations are hypothetical and use invented figures. |
| Computation (baseline) document hinting that anything modifies it | **none.** *Charge for Analyst Hours Beyond the Pool* states "No grace allowance is set against the chargeable hours" and "The analyst hour rate is the rate the tier sets for analyst hours beyond the included pool" flatly; *The Sum that Clears a Subscription* states "No settlement allowance is granted against the amount owed" and "The credits set against it are every credit standing on the subscription" flatly. | Factor document naming, overriding or pointing at the computation document or another factor | **none.** Each of the nine names only the quantity it decides and the records its tiers rest on. |

Both hops of this task's tree were marked **state-derived** in the blind answer; none was pre-solved, so nothing is carried here from Step 2.
